items.title: IRGC claims attacks on oil tankers, ships and US vessels
items.summary: IRGC claims attacks on oil tankers, ships and US vessels Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said it targeted several vessels that attempted to pass through what it described as the "forbidden and unsafe area" of ​​the Strait of Hormuz. According to the IRGC's latest statement, its navy attacked and "caused great damage" to two American vessels and eight oil tankers in retaliation to earlier US strikes on Iranian vessels. It also targeted 10 "violating ships", that it said were "attempting to pass through the prohibited and unsafe area of ​​the Strait of Hormuz, with the instigation and support of the invading terrorist army of the United States". "The Strait of Hormuz is under the strong and powerful surveillance and management of the capable and brave naval force of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps," it added.

items.title: Tehran condemns US attacks on Iranian commercial vessels
items.summary: Tehran condemns US attacks on Iranian commercial vessels Iran’s foreign ministry has condemned a US attack on Iranian commercial vessels in the Persian Gulf and the Gulf of Oman on Saturday. In a statement, the ministry said the strikes were “a continuation of the US military aggression against Iran”, adding that it constituted a "clear violation" of a clause in the "United Nations Charter, a war crime, and an overt threat to international peace and the security of commercial shipping". The ministry asserted that Tehran remains determined to "firmly defend its sovereignty and national interests" against US actions, including Washington's ongoing maritime blockade, attacks on commercial vessels, and its continued "economic war". "The Ministry of Foreign Affairs stresses that responsibility for the consequences arising from the continuation of US aggressive and interventionist actions in the region will rest with the US regime and its accomplices and partners," it added.

items.title: US strikes perimeter of Iran’s Bushehr nuclear plant, Iranian state media reports
items.summary: US strikes perimeter of Iran’s Bushehr nuclear plant, Iranian state media reports The United States targeted the perimeter of Iran’s Bushehr nuclear power plant on Thursday, Iranian state media reported, citing Ehsan Jahanian, deputy governor of Bushehr province. Jahanian said several areas across the province were targeted, including the area around the nuclear plant, a military base in the town of Choghadak and a fishing pier in southern Bushehr. He said there were no immediate reports of casualties. Residents in Choghadak, located just over 20km (12 miles) from the Bushehr plant, reported hearing several explosions. The Bushehr facility, Iran’s only civilian nuclear power plant, has previously been affected by strikes in the area during the ongoing Middle East war.

items.summary: IRGC warns it will target oil tankers in Kuwait, Bahrain after US attack The IRGC navy warned on Tuesday that it will target oil tankers in the vicinity of Kuwaiti and Bahraini ports in response to recent US attacks on Iranian oil tankers. In a message carried by Iranian broadcaster IRIB, the IRGC navy urged the crew of oil tankers in the vicinity of Kuwaiti and Bahraini ports to immediately leave their vessels, whether anchored or docked. This comes after a spokesperson for the Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters, Iran’s joint military ⁠command, said earlier on Tuesday that Iranian forces will “heavily target” US bases and other interests in the region if the US military attacks any Iranian ships, adding that the US military has threatened to target three Iranian oil tankers, in comments carried by Iranian broadcaster IRIB.

items.title: US diesel prices hit record $5.85 a gallon
items.summary: US diesel prices hit record $5.85 a gallon The price of diesel hit a new record Friday in the United States, as disruption from the US war with Iran squeezes voters. The cost is now $5.85 a gallon, up from $3.71 a year ago, the AAA motorists' association said. Diesel is used by farmers to run equipment, and it also powers the trucks needed to bring food to grocery stores. US farmers faced a double whammy of surging fertiliser and diesel prices as the spring planting season got underway. The Independent Grocers Alliance estimates that fuel-related costs can account for 15 to 30 percent of the total cost for some food products. Besides diesel, the cost of regular gasoline is also notably higher at an average of $4.15 per gallon, compared with $3.20 last year. (Reporting by AFP)

items.summary: US diesel prices hit all-time high because of Iran war Drivers in the US are paying more than ever for diesel at the pump as the US-Israeli war on Iran continues to hit ordinary citizens at home. In the US, diesel is mostly used by commercial vehicles, such as trucks, trains, boats, buses, farming vehicles and construction vehicles, the BBC reported. The average price for one gallon of diesel in the US has hit $5.85, compared to an average of $3.71 a year ago and above the previous high following Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine, the American Automobile Association said. Fuel prices have soared since the US and Israel launched their war on Iran at the end of February, reflecting the surge in wholesale oil prices. In response to rising fuel costs, US President Donald Trump recently pledged to “substantially lower Gas Prices for all Americans” through an oil deal with Venezuela, after the US kidnapped the country's former president Nicolas Maduro then supported his successor Delcy Rodriguez.

items.title: ‘One day the Taliban will need women to be educated’: three sisters on being forced back to Afghanistan
items.summary: Shallah, Fatimah and Maahi are among hundreds of thousands of Afghan women and girls deported from Iran and Pakistan in the past year to a life of severe restrictions It was a warm summer afternoon on 15 August 2021 when the Taliban entered Kabul and changed the lives of millions. Shallah*, then 16, watched the news at home on the Afghan TV channel Tolo news. She ran crying to the garden, to tell her mother that Afghanistan had fallen. Her younger sister, Fatimah*, then 11, was at her cousin’s house, where her aunt told her the news. At the time, she says, she did not understand what a takeover meant, or who the Taliban were. Her elder sister, Maahi*, then 22, was well aware of the consequences and remembers her hands shaking at work as she read the news on her phone, on Facebook pages of Afghan news. Continue reading...

clusters.headline: Vat olie boven de 100 dollar, ook benzineprijs blijft stijgen

items.title: Vat olie boven de 100 dollar, ook benzineprijs blijft stijgen
items.summary: Na de nieuwe aanvallen van de Verenigde Staten en Iran zijn de olieprijzen opnieuw gestegen. De prijs van een vat Brent-olie kwam vanochtend boven de 100 dollar uit. Dat is voor het eerst sinds juli. Een vat Brent-olie is inmiddels bijna 60 procent duurder dan begin dit jaar. Door de aanvallen tussen de Verenigde Staten en Iran is er onrust op de oliemarkt. Het aanhoudende geweld vergroot de zorgen over mogelijke verstoringen van de olie-export uit de regio. De Amerikaanse bank Goldman Sachs heeft gewaarschuwd dat de olieprijs kan oplopen naar 120 dollar per vat als de aanvallen aanhouden. De stijgende olieprijs is ook al te merken aan de pomp. De adviesprijs voor een liter benzine ligt nu rond de 2,72 euro.

clusters.headline: Transition énergétique: la facture de l'après-pétrole sera lourde pour les pétro-États

items.title: Transition énergétique: la facture de l'après-pétrole sera lourde pour les pétro-États
items.summary: La sortie mondiale du pétrole pourrait entraîner des conflits, des migrations et des bouleversements économiques selon une étude du groupe de réflexion E3G publiée mardi 8 septembre. L’utilisation du pétrole est en déclin dans de nombreux pays, avec la croissance des énergies renouvelables, et les effets de la guerre en Iran qui a limité l’offre et fait flamber les prix. Et cette stagnation va obliger les producteurs à rechercher un bassin d’acheteurs en déclin. Des pays comme le Nigeria, l’Iran, l’Angola et l’Algérie font partie des pays qui seront gravement touchés, car ils dépendent fortement des revenus pétroliers pour financer leurs services publics. Sans aide internationale, ils ne pourront pas amortir le choc alertent les experts.

items.summary: Het Amerikaanse vliegdekschip USS Abraham Lincoln is na vijf dagen vertrokken uit Thailand. Bijna 5000 bemanningsleden zijn meer dan negen maanden na hun vertrek uit de Verenigde Staten onderweg naar de haven van San Diego. De afgelopen vijf dagen lag de Lincoln in de Thaise haven Laem Chabang, dicht bij de badplaats Pattaya. De badplaats is Amerikaanse soldaten niet onbekend: tijdens de Vietnamoorlog werd het een bekende plek voor het zogenoemde R&R ( Rest and Relaxation) , oftewel: een vakantie voor militairen. De badplaats had daarvoor voorbereidingen getroffen: er werd onder meer een prostitutieverbod ingesteld en er werden extra agenten ingezet. Lokale verslaggevers melden dat het bezoek relatief soepel is verlopen. Soldaten genoten van voetspa's, winkelen en roomservice. Volgens persbureau AFP zijn twee leden van het leger teruggestuurd naar het schip na een dronken ruzie. items.summary: U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner will reportedly travel to Moscow and Kyiv this weekend in an effort to revive negotiations to end the war in Ukraine. It will mark the diplomatic duo’s first trip to Kyiv since President Donald Trump’s return to office, and follows CIA director John Ratcliffe’s visit to Moscow last week. “It is unclear whether the Americans are bringing new proposals to the two presidents, or are pushing them to close the gap on the remaining issues, which include who will ultimately control the Donbas, Ukrainian territory that is partly occupied by Russia,” according to a New York Times report. George Beebe, director of grand strategy at the Quincy Institute, called the development “most welcome” and said all parties had strong reasons to find a way to end the fighting. He cautioned, however, that “seizing this propitious moment will require overcoming deep mistrust between the two countries” and addressing doubt that the “Trump administration has the political clout and persistence to overcome opposition in Europe and inside the Washington establishment.”

items.summary: Witkoff and Kushner to visit Russia and Ukraine at weekend, says Tass US negotiators Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner will visit Russia and Ukraine on Saturday and Sunday, Russian news agency Tass reported, citing a source. There was no immediate confirmation. Witkoff and Kushner last visited Moscow in January, when they held four hours of late-night talks with President Vladimir Putin in the Kremlin, Reuters reported. The two men are also US President Donald Trump's lead negotiators on Gaza and the war on Iran. If the visit takes place it will be their first to Kyiv. “The Russians don't want them to visit Kyiv and are trying to make them change the plan,” the source told the Russian news agency. The last US-mediated talks between Russia and Ukraine took place in February, shortly before the United States and Israel launched their war on Iran.

In totaal werd er 21,8 miljoen ton vervoerd. Dat is het laagste vervoerde gewicht in de maand augustus in de afgelopen vijftien jaar. In augustus bedroeg het gemiddelde gewicht per schip zo'n 1299 ton, terwijl dat normaal rond de 1500 ton ligt. Het is niet de eerste keer dat het vervoerde gewicht in de binnenvaart fors afneemt door lage waterstanden: dit gebeurde in 2018 en 2022 ook. Er ging bijna 40 procent minder gewicht aan goederen naar Duitsland, en omgekeerd kwam er voor een kleine 50 procent minder naar Nederland. These include everything from his seeming “war on DEI” within the department, to combative engagements with members of Congress, to shade being thrown even by President Donald Trump himself on the lack of success in the (second) Iran War. In truth, most people in the United States don’t think about Ukraine much these days. items.title: 25 jaar na de aanslagen van 9/11 zet Trump het mes in terreurbestrijding
items.summary: Sinds 11 september 2001 zijn er geen grootschalige terroristische aanslagen meer geweest in de Verenigde Staten. Maar experts maken zich grote zorgen of Amerika 25 jaar later nog steeds 'op scherp' staat, nu president Trump het mes heeft gezet in delen van de terrorismebestrijding. "Schokkend en frustrerend", noemt voormalig terrorismebestrijder Michael Duffin het, die vorig jaar werd ontslagen. "Het maakt ons minder veilig." In september 2001 was Duffin net afgestudeerd. Hij volgde de aanslagen op de Twin Towers in New York en het Pentagon bij Washington op televisie. "Ik wilde begrijpen wat er was gebeurd. Ik vroeg me af: kan ik een rol spelen in het voorkomen van een nieuwe aanslag zoals 9/11?" En dus ging hij werken bij het Bureau voor Terrorismebestrijding. Forse investeringen De voorloper daarvan werd opgericht in de jaren 70, na de aanslagen op de Olympische Spelen in München. Na 11 september 2001 werd flink opgeschaald. items.title: US war on Iran: 'Incompetent administration when it comes to negotiations and prosecuting war'
items.summary: Mark Owen is pleased to welcome Barbara Slavin, Distinguished Fellow at the Simpson Center. She frames the war in the Persian Gulf as a mutually damaging stalemate in which neither Washington nor Tehran has found a politically sustainable exit: "There are no winners in this war". Her central argument is that the conflict has created a problem of face-saving as much as military strategy. The US faces rising economic and electoral costs, while Iran confronts shortages, inflation, domestic dissent and intensified repression. Neither side, in her assessment, can plausibly claim success.

items.title: Peace in Ukraine remains far off despite Witkoff-Kushner effort

They then traveled to Kyiv for talks with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, who said the pair presented him with some "worthwhile ideas." Yet, as the war drags closer to five full years of fighting, chances of success at the negotiating table appear slim. Don’t hold your breath for an end to the Ukraine war before the midterms in November. More likely, Putin will continue to shift the goalposts until he achieves his core goals: Ukrainian neutrality and the political decapitation of Zelensky. More than a year has passed since President Donald Trump met with Putin in Anchorage. The Trump Administration has been unable to deliver upon the compromises offered at that summit. items.summary: Twenty-five years ago, 19 hijackers took control of four American airliners and crashed them into symbols of American power, killing upwards of 3000 people. The American population watched the events unfold in real time. It was an emotionally jarring event that changed the country. In some respects, the events of 9/11 needed no explanation. The destruction of the World Trade Center buildings and the massive, and random, loss of life were horrifying to all. The meaning of the attacks, however – and the motivations of the hijackers – were less clear. The effort to explain the motives behind the attack, and to understand “why they hate us,” brought a pre-existing debate over Islamist militancy to the center of American public life. In the decade leading up to 9/11, the Washington policy community had been divided over how to deal with the Islamist movement and particularly those extremists who sought to use violence to impose a narrow vision of religious orthodoxy upon reluctant societies. items.summary: From the start, the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran has been a story of unintended consequences. Contrary to President Donald Trump’s hopes for a quick victory, the conflict has morphed into a sustained crisis, one that has driven up oil prices, driven down tourism in the Middle East, and reshaped the region’s geopolitical map. Now, a new unintended consequence has emerged: the return of piracy to Somalia’s coasts. This shift, which comes after a decade of quiet, threatens some of the world’s most important shipping lanes and the interests of the United States and its allies. Pirates have attacked at least 15 vessels in the region this year, a sharp uptick from the five attacks that occurred last year, according to data from the International Maritime Organization. The renewed criminal activity has led to extended hostage situations, including one ongoing seizure of an oil tanker and its crew. The IAEA has been unable to access several key Iranian nuclear sites since Israel, later joined by the US, launched a 12-day conflict in June 2025 that included strikes on nuclear facilities. Sites have also been hit in the latest war, which began on 28 February, prompting repeated calls from the agency for renewed access. “The best, shortest way for a positive outcome is for Iran to engage with us,” Grossi told reporters after opening the IAEA Board of Governors’ quarterly meeting. clusters.headline: Iran warns of retaliation if IAEA adopts resolution against Tehran

items.title: Iran warns of retaliation if IAEA adopts resolution against Tehran
items.summary: Iran warns of retaliation if IAEA adopts resolution against Tehran Iran has warned that it will take reciprocal action if the UN nuclear watchdog adopts a resolution against Tehran, foreign ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei said on Monday. Speaking at a press briefing, Baghaei criticised European states seeking a resolution against Iran, calling their approach “irrational” given that the ongoing US-Iran war has made several Iranian nuclear facilities inaccessible to international inspectors. His comments come as the US, Britain, France and Germany push for a resolution at the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) over Iran’s lack of cooperation and access to its nuclear sites. Iran has restricted IAEA access to facilities affected by previous strikes, arguing that normal safeguarding arrangements have become impractical under wartime conditions. The dispute has deepened concerns over the status of Iran’s enriched uranium stockpile and the international community’s ability to verify the nature of its nuclear programme.

items.summary: Rund ein halbes Jahr vor der Präsidentschaftswahl droht Frankreich zum Stresstest für die Eurozone zu werden: Politische Krise, angespannte Haushaltslage und wachsende Zweifel der Märkte an der Fähigkeit des Landes, seine wachsende Schuldenlast zu finanzieren, treffen zusammen.  Frankreich hat ein tiefes Ungleichgewicht der öffentlichen Finanzen. Das Haushaltsdefizit übersteigt 5 Prozent des BIP , die Staatsquote liegt bei etwa 57 Prozent . Gleichzeitig steigt die Staatsverschuldung stetig an und könnte, ohne ausreichende Konsolidierungsmaßnahmen, bis 2030 sogar 130 Prozent des BIP überschreiten . Die Zinslast der öffentlichen Verschuldung steigt rasant  und könnte bis 2030 auf über 120 Milliarden Euro oder 3,5 Prozent des BIP steigen. Das größte Problem könnte sich jedoch nicht in der reinen Haushaltsarithmetik zeigen, sondern in der politischen Fähigkeit, diese zu ändern. Einerseits sind die Kosten des Sozialsystems nicht mehr tragfähig, andererseits fordert die Mehrheit der Bevölkerung weiterhin ein Eingreifen des Staates. When addressing what he planned to do next, he joked that “you could scan my head” for an answer and still come up empty because he had not yet decided himself. One possibility, however, was firmly off the table: another run for Congress. Massie said he once held out hope that Congress could fix itself. His years inside the institution had convinced him otherwise. The energy with which he was received was indicative of his standing at the conference and within the broader antiwar movement. items.summary: Iran turns to land trade routes to counter maritime blockade We have more from Iran’s top security official, Mohsen Rezaei. Rezaei says Tehran has started activating overland trade corridors to reduce its dependence on shipping and counter the maritime blockade. He pointed to Iran’s borders with 15 neighbouring countries, arguing that its geographical position gives it alternatives to sea-based commerce. Rezaei also said Iran and Oman had agreed on a new international corridor through the Strait of Hormuz, which Tehran would oversee. “The new international corridor that Iran manages has been determined with the Omani brothers and will be announced in the coming days,” Rezaei said, according to state media.

clusters.headline: The Falklands dispute: What’s it got to do with Israel and the US?

items.title: The Falklands dispute: What’s it got to do with Israel and the US?
items.summary: The Falklands dispute: What’s it got to do with Israel and the US? Argentina has restated its claim to sovereignty over the Falkland Islands, a small rocky archipelago in the South Atlantic that is owned by the UK . Javier Milei, the far-right president of Argentina, said in a national address on Thursday that the "winds of change" favoured his country’s claim to the islands, and threatened sanctions on oil firms that seek to drill in the territory’s waters. "We need to recover these islands which are nationally relevant," he said. The announcement comes days after US President Donald Trump suggested that he is reviewing the US position on UK sovereignty, known in Argentina as Las Islas Malvinas. “I always review every position - that’s just one of many,” Trump told reporters in the White House. “The UK’s got some problems, but they’ll get solved." The future of the sparsely inhabited islands has been speculated on for months amid tensions between Washington and London about UK military commitments, including the war on Iran . items.summary: Está lejos, Amritsar. Miles de kilómetros separan la capital española de esta ciudad de la India, en la que se levanta el corazón espiritual del sijismo, una religión nacida de un acercamiento de posturas entre el hinduismo y el islam. Cada día, los sij de esta región se reúnen para comer en la monumental infraestructura que constituye el Templo Dorado, donde llenan sus bandejas sin coste ni distinción por edad, género o religión. Lo mismo sucede, en proporciones contenidas, en una nave industrial de Villaverde que esconde el único templo sij de la capital, el Gurudwara Nanaksar Sahib de Madrid. Con el mismo espíritu que en la India, pero en esplendor y dimensiones reducidos, este lugar ofrece comidas gratuitas cada domingo a unas pocas decenas de personas.Laura, madrileña de Las Rozas y bautizada en el catolicismo, es una habitual en el lugar desde que, hace más de un año, un viaje a la India despertó en ella una nueva forma de concebir su fe. «Aquí aprendo cómo llegar a dios, que es el mismo para todos», sostiene. items.summary: Fresh Yemen clashes kill more than 60, including 26 soldiers Fighting between Yemen's Saudi-backed government forces and the country's Houthi rebels killed more than 60 people on Saturday, including civilians, medical and military sources told AFP. The renewed clashes in Yemen's southwest over control of a gateway to the Red Sea came after Friday saw some of the deadliest fighting in years, following the collapse in July of a 2022 ceasefire. items.title: El nuevo líder iraní en la sombra, Rezai: «Mejor el cierre de Ormuz que tener una docena de bombas atómicas»
items.summary: Sin pruebas de que Mojtaba Jamenei aún vive y manda, cada facción del aparato de Teherán puede alegar que eso es lo que el Líder Supremo le ha dicho que haga. Pero nadie sabe con total seguridad quién toma las principales decisiones en Irán. El Gobierno está presidido por Pezeshkian. Las negociaciones indirectas con los estadounidenses las dirige el presidente del Parlamento, Ghalibaf. Four vessels entered the Middle East Gulf and one exited, using a mix of Iranian, Omani and negotiated routes. Two of the crossings involved shadow vessels, while one involved a sanctioned vessel. Kpler said the figure remained preliminary, noting that additional “dark” crossings could be retrospectively identified and added as new confirmation data becomes available. Activity through the Bab el-Mandeb was comparatively stable, with 35 confirmed crossings, up 2.9 percent day on day. Nineteen vessels entered the Red Sea and 16 exited. No dark transits were recorded, while the International Maritime Organization verified no additional attacks. clusters.headline: World food prices at highest since 2022, says UN

items.title: World food prices at highest since 2022, says UN
items.summary: World food prices at highest since 2022, says UN World food prices rose in August to their highest since late 2022, impacted partly by the war on Iran, the United Nations' Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) said on Friday. Extreme heat and drought in Europe, the threat of a severe El Nino weather pattern and trade upheaval caused by the Ukraine and Iran wars have unsettled agricultural markets, pushing grain prices to three-year highs and sugar to a one-year peak, the agency said. The FAO Food Price Index, which tracks monthly changes in a basket of internationally traded food commodities, averaged 133.3 points in August, up from July's revised reading of 130.8. That was the highest score since November 2022, though nearly 17 percent below a record peak from March 2022, after Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine, Reuters reported. Escalating attacks in the Black Sea have curtailed grain shipments from Russia and Ukraine, while the war on Iran is still straining flows of fertiliser for crops.

clusters.headline: Adam Telle appointed as acting US Army Secretary, Trump says

items.title: Adam Telle appointed as acting US Army Secretary, Trump says
items.summary: Adam Telle appointed as acting US Army Secretary, Trump says US President Donald Trump said that he was appointing Adam Telle, assistant secretary of the Army for civil works, as the acting US Army Secretary. This came after the White House confirmed earlier this week that former army secretary, Dan Driscoll, submitted his resignation. Driscoll’s departure came following reports of increasing tensions with Secretary of War Pete Hegseth as well as signs of unease in the Pentagon over how the Trump administration is prosecuting the war on Iran. The heads of the army, navy and air force, and the four-star commanders overseeing US operations throughout Europe, Asia and Latin America, have warned Hegseth that any prolonging of major operations would weaken the Washington's ability to confront other foes, the Washington Post reported on Monday.

clusters.headline: Iran says oil industry circumventing US blockade

items.title: Iran says oil industry circumventing US blockade
items.summary: Iran says oil industry circumventing US blockade Iran’s oil industry continues to find ways around a US military blockade of the country’s ports and vessels, Petroleum Minister Mohsen Paknejad told the Iranian Students News Agency (ISNA). “We are pursuing various strategies and have taken measures to overcome the blockade,” Paknejad said, describing the situation as difficult. He said US forces had attacked Kharg Island off Iran’s southwestern coast “more than 550 times” during the first 40 days of the conflict. Iran exported about 90 percent of its crude oil from the island before the war.

The night of 4-5 August, an airport bus driver discovered an armed drone lying near the tarmac of the Leipzig-Halle airport, which is a central hub of Europe’s logistical support to Ukraine’s war effort. A cargo jet, meanwhile, may have struck a second drone shortly after takeoff, forcing an abrupt landing, and investigators found a third drone laden with military explosives nearby. In 2024, incendiary devices hidden in parcels ignited in DHL cargo at the same airport. Had these detonated in the air, a major air catastrophe and large-scale civilian casualties would have ensued, probably resulting in a broader war. Continue reading...

clusters.headline: ‘I would rather die than return to France’: the brutal reality of the UK’s one in, one out scheme

items.title: ‘I would rather die than return to France’: the brutal reality of the UK’s one in, one out scheme
items.summary: Aso and Baran fled Iran, crossed the Channel together and were both returned to France. After risking their lives to reach Britain again, the friends found themselves facing very different fates At the end of last year, two men fled Iran. Aso and Baran* were strangers at the time. The way their stories would cross, then diverge, reveals the cruel arbitrariness of the UK asylum system in general, and the government’s controversial one in, one out scheme in particular. Before he left Iran, Aso, 28, had converted from Islam to Christianity, putting his life in imminent danger. “I had to keep my conversion to Christianity a secret,” he says. “I knew if I was caught, I risked being executed by the Iranian regime … one of my relatives, who I trusted, paid smugglers to get me out last November.” Continue reading...

items.title: 'Inappropriate to say': Trump may still be considering CIA-led uprising in Iran
items.summary: 'Inappropriate to say': Trump may still be considering CIA-led uprising in Iran US President Donald Trump on Wednesday said it "wouldn't be appropriate to say" if he would greenlight the CIA arming Iranians to encourage a violent uprising, a day after he asked on his TruthSocial account, "When are the Iranian people going to rise up and fight?" Trump was taking unscheduled questions in the Oval Office, after the US unleashed a barrage of strikes on Iran's southern coast on Tuesday, killing 18 people, including two children at a wedding. "Will you send the CIA in to arm Iranians?" a reporter asked the president. "I'd love to tell you that, but it wouldn't be appropriate to say," Trump responded. "But I mean, I understand their plight. They're being shot... They have close to 65,000 protesters killed." It remains unclear where that figure is sourced, given Trump has previously floated figures between 25,000 and 80,000 during the anti-government protests in Iran early this year. Read more: 'Inappropriate to say': Trump may still be considering CIA-led uprising in Iran

Van januari tot en met augustus werden ruim 22.000 leningen verstrekt. In heel 2025 waren dat er 21.000. De lening wordt gebruikt voor bijvoorbeeld muur- en dakisolatie, isolerend glas of zonnepanelen. Als tegenzet gooide Iran de Straat van Hormuz dicht, de zeestraat waardoor tot die tijd een vijfde van de wereldwijde olie en aardgas werd vervoerd. Door die blokkade zijn de energieprijzen fors gestegen. "De piek was vanaf het moment dat de oorlog begon", vertelt Katinka Huiberts, bestuurslid bij het Nationaal Warmtefonds. "De aanvragen begonnen toen heel scherp te stijgen." Die stijging zette het hele voorjaar tot de zomer door, zegt Huiberts. clusters.headline: Por qué el país más rico del mundo no puede defender sus infraestructuras vitales

items.title: Por qué el país más rico del mundo no puede defender sus infraestructuras vitales
items.summary: El agua es una vulnerabilidad estratégica, un hecho que no es ninguna novedad para los mandos militares. Cuando los ostrogodos quisieron paralizar Roma en el año 537, destruyeron sus acueductos. Más recientemente, las infraestructuras hidráulicas han sido un objetivo importante en el conflicto de Estados Unidos con Irán, a pesar de que las leyes internacionales clasifican este tipo de ataques como posibles crímenes de guerra. En marzo, Donald Trump amenazó con «destruir por completo… posiblemente todas» las instalaciones de desalinización de Irán, que son esenciales para la vida en las áridas provincias del sur del país. Morgen stijgt de benzineprijs dus verder. UnitedConsumers berekent de gemiddelde adviesprijs dagelijks op basis van de prijzen van de vijf grote aanbieders: Shell, BP, Texaco, Esso en TotalEnergies. clusters.headline: Gulf states struggle to recover economically after 6 months of war

items.title: Gulf states struggle to recover economically after 6 months of war
items.summary: The Persian Gulf’s extraordinary wealth has long rested on an assumption of stability. The past six months of war have shattered that certainty, exposing a fundamental weakness in Gulf economic models: producing oil and gas is only half the equation when infrastructure and access to global markets can be disrupted. Ports, airports, power grids, desalination plants, financial centers, and tourism hubs are all vulnerable to the same regional shocks. The energy sector is particularly exposed, with damaged oil and gas facilities potentially taking months or longer to repair. Yet restoring production may prove easier than restoring confidence that Gulf exports can reliably reach global markets. Each Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) state enters this new era from a different starting point. Qatar, Kuwait and Bahrain are particularly exposed because of their reliance on Gulf maritime routes, including the Strait of Hormuz. The US-Israeli assault has caused oil prices to spike amid Iran's closure of the vital strait of Hormuz shipping lane, although prices are now far lower than at the height of hostilities earlier this year, when crude traded at upwards of $110 per barrel.

items.summary: The signing on 7 August of the so-called Mecca Pact by Saudi Arabia, Türkiye and Pakistan again raises the question of whether the Gulf monarchies might seek to reduce their security dependence on the United States. The Gulf monarchies’ experience of the Iran war makes such a realignment appear plausible. Despite their decades-long partnership with Washington, they became targets of Iranian drone and missile attacks that caused considerable damage to the region’s energy infrastructure and severely disrupted energy exports, as the Strait of Hormuz was effectively closed. The Trump administration appears to have taken little account of their security interests . Nevertheless, three factors make an end to their close ties with Washington unlikely. Limits of realignment First, the Gulf monarchies have no viable alternative to the United States as a security guarantor. For all their differences in foreign and security policy, they share a common predicament: None of their other partners is willing or able to take Washington’s place. Prima dell’inizio della guerra, l’isola di Kharg gestiva la maggior parte delle esportazioni petrolifere iraniane, rappresentando un nodo strategico per l’economia di Teheran. items.summary: When President Donald Trump congratulated Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan for signing the Mecca Pact, describing it as a “BIG, BOLD, IMPORTANT FIRST STEP,” he was not simply trafficking in diplomatic pleasantries. The Trump administration also tacitly endorsed a multilateral, Saudi-led maritime initiative to protect shipping in the Red Sea, sending senior U.S. military officials to the meeting where the arrangement was agreed to. The thread running through both initiatives is clear: regional states taking greater responsibility for their own security. Behind Trump’s flattery, something more important appears to be taking shape. According to Pentagon planning reported by the Washington Post, the Defense Department is exploring a broader reduction of its forces in the Persian Gulf, which would entail moving units, command centers and aerial capabilities west toward Jordan, Israel and Saudi Arabia’s Red Sea coast. items.title: La modernité de l’Iranienne Forough Farrokhzâd, poétesse rebelle et lumineuse
items.summary: Forough Farrokhzâd est l’une des plus grandes figures de la poésie iranienne du dernier siècle. Sa disparition brutale en 1967, à l’âge de 32 ans, fut une perte immense pour son pays, pour la littérature. Sa voix, « fusionnée dans les atomes du temps » comme elle l’a écrit, continue de se faire entendre à travers sa poésie sublime et tragique. « J’irai jusqu’au rivage du soleil » est le titre du volume en traduction française de ses poésies complètes, paru cette année dans la prestigieuse collection Poésie/Gallimard.

items.title: ‘One day the Taliban will need women to be educated’: three sisters on being forced back to Afghanistan
items.summary: Shallah, Fatimah and Maahi are among hundreds of thousands of Afghan women and girls deported from Iran and Pakistan in the past year to a life of severe restrictions It was a warm summer afternoon on 15 August 2021 when the Taliban entered Kabul and changed the lives of millions. Shallah*, then 16, watched the news at home on the Afghan TV channel Tolo news. She ran crying to the garden, to tell her mother that Afghanistan had fallen. Her younger sister, Fatimah*, then 11, was at her cousin’s house, where her aunt told her the news. At the time, she says, she did not understand what a takeover meant, or who the Taliban were. Her elder sister, Maahi*, then 22, was well aware of the consequences and remembers her hands shaking at work as she read the news on her phone, on Facebook pages of Afghan news. Continue reading...

items.title: Vat olie boven de 100 dollar, ook benzineprijs blijft stijgen
items.summary: Na de nieuwe aanvallen van de Verenigde Staten en Iran zijn de olieprijzen opnieuw gestegen. De prijs van een vat Brent-olie kwam vanochtend boven de 100 dollar uit. Dat is voor het eerst sinds juli. Een vat Brent-olie is inmiddels bijna 60 procent duurder dan begin dit jaar. Door de aanvallen tussen de Verenigde Staten en Iran is er onrust op de oliemarkt. Het aanhoudende geweld vergroot de zorgen over mogelijke verstoringen van de olie-export uit de regio. De Amerikaanse bank Goldman Sachs heeft gewaarschuwd dat de olieprijs kan oplopen naar 120 dollar per vat als de aanvallen aanhouden. De stijgende olieprijs is ook al te merken aan de pomp. De adviesprijs voor een liter benzine ligt nu rond de 2,72 euro.

items.title: Transition énergétique: la facture de l'après-pétrole sera lourde pour les pétro-États
items.summary: La sortie mondiale du pétrole pourrait entraîner des conflits, des migrations et des bouleversements économiques selon une étude du groupe de réflexion E3G publiée mardi 8 septembre. L’utilisation du pétrole est en déclin dans de nombreux pays, avec la croissance des énergies renouvelables, et les effets de la guerre en Iran qui a limité l’offre et fait flamber les prix. Et cette stagnation va obliger les producteurs à rechercher un bassin d’acheteurs en déclin. Des pays comme le Nigeria, l’Iran, l’Angola et l’Algérie font partie des pays qui seront gravement touchés, car ils dépendent fortement des revenus pétroliers pour financer leurs services publics. Sans aide internationale, ils ne pourront pas amortir le choc alertent les experts.

items.summary: De lage waterstanden deze zomer waren een groot probleem voor de binnenvaart. In augustus is er bijna 19 procent minder gewicht aan goederen vervoerd dan een jaar eerder. Dat blijkt uit cijfers van het Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek (CBS). Door de aanhoudende droogte daalde de vaardiepte, waardoor schepen minder zwaar beladen konden worden. In totaal werd er 21,8 miljoen ton vervoerd. Dat is het laagste vervoerde gewicht in de maand augustus in de afgelopen vijftien jaar. In augustus bedroeg het gemiddelde gewicht per schip zo'n 1299 ton, terwijl dat normaal rond de 1500 ton ligt. Het is niet de eerste keer dat het vervoerde gewicht in de binnenvaart fors afneemt door lage waterstanden: dit gebeurde in 2018 en 2022 ook. Verschillen Naar bijna elk land werd er minder vervoerd via de binnenvaart. Het vervoer tussen Nederland en Duitsland nam het sterkst af. Er ging bijna 40 procent minder gewicht aan goederen naar Duitsland, en omgekeerd kwam er voor een kleine 50 procent minder naar Nederland. items.title: Trump denials can't hide billions in US weapons sent to Ukraine

In truth, most people in the United States don’t think about Ukraine much these days. items.title: Tehran condemns US attacks on Iranian commercial vessels
items.summary: Tehran condemns US attacks on Iranian commercial vessels Iran’s foreign ministry has condemned a US attack on Iranian commercial vessels in the Persian Gulf and the Gulf of Oman on Saturday. In a statement, the ministry said the strikes were “a continuation of the US military aggression against Iran”, adding that it constituted a "clear violation" of a clause in the "United Nations Charter, a war crime, and an overt threat to international peace and the security of commercial shipping". The ministry asserted that Tehran remains determined to "firmly defend its sovereignty and national interests" against US actions, including Washington's ongoing maritime blockade, attacks on commercial vessels, and its continued "economic war". "The Ministry of Foreign Affairs stresses that responsibility for the consequences arising from the continuation of US aggressive and interventionist actions in the region will rest with the US regime and its accomplices and partners," it added.

items.title: 25 jaar na de aanslagen van 9/11 zet Trump het mes in terreurbestrijding

Maar experts maken zich grote zorgen of Amerika 25 jaar later nog steeds 'op scherp' staat, nu president Trump het mes heeft gezet in delen van de terrorismebestrijding. "Schokkend en frustrerend", noemt voormalig terrorismebestrijder Michael Duffin het, die vorig jaar werd ontslagen. "Het maakt ons minder veilig." In september 2001 was Duffin net afgestudeerd. Hij volgde de aanslagen op de Twin Towers in New York en het Pentagon bij Washington op televisie. "Ik wilde begrijpen wat er was gebeurd. Ik vroeg me af: kan ik een rol spelen in het voorkomen van een nieuwe aanslag zoals 9/11?" En dus ging hij werken bij het Bureau voor Terrorismebestrijding. Forse investeringen De voorloper daarvan werd opgericht in de jaren 70, na de aanslagen op de Olympische Spelen in München. Na 11 september 2001 werd flink opgeschaald. items.title: US war on Iran: 'Incompetent administration when it comes to negotiations and prosecuting war'
items.summary: Mark Owen is pleased to welcome Barbara Slavin, Distinguished Fellow at the Simpson Center. She frames the war in the Persian Gulf as a mutually damaging stalemate in which neither Washington nor Tehran has found a politically sustainable exit: "There are no winners in this war". Her central argument is that the conflict has created a problem of face-saving as much as military strategy. The US faces rising economic and electoral costs, while Iran confronts shortages, inflation, domestic dissent and intensified repression. Neither side, in her assessment, can plausibly claim success.

Yet, as the war drags closer to five full years of fighting, chances of success at the negotiating table appear slim. Don’t hold your breath for an end to the Ukraine war before the midterms in November. More likely, Putin will continue to shift the goalposts until he achieves his core goals: Ukrainian neutrality and the political decapitation of Zelensky. items.title: 25 years after 9/11, the US still doesn't know 'why they hate us'
items.summary: Twenty-five years ago, 19 hijackers took control of four American airliners and crashed them into symbols of American power, killing upwards of 3000 people. The American population watched the events unfold in real time. It was an emotionally jarring event that changed the country. In some respects, the events of 9/11 needed no explanation. The destruction of the World Trade Center buildings and the massive, and random, loss of life were horrifying to all. The meaning of the attacks, however – and the motivations of the hijackers – were less clear. The effort to explain the motives behind the attack, and to understand “why they hate us,” brought a pre-existing debate over Islamist militancy to the center of American public life. items.title: Somali piracy was under control. Then came the Iran war.
items.summary: From the start, the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran has been a story of unintended consequences. Contrary to President Donald Trump’s hopes for a quick victory, the conflict has morphed into a sustained crisis, one that has driven up oil prices, driven down tourism in the Middle East, and reshaped the region’s geopolitical map. Now, a new unintended consequence has emerged: the return of piracy to Somalia’s coasts. This shift, which comes after a decade of quiet, threatens some of the world’s most important shipping lanes and the interests of the United States and its allies. Pirates have attacked at least 15 vessels in the region this year, a sharp uptick from the five attacks that occurred last year, according to data from the International Maritime Organization. The renewed criminal activity has led to extended hostage situations, including one ongoing seizure of an oil tanker and its crew. items.title: US strikes perimeter of Iran’s Bushehr nuclear plant, Iranian state media reports
items.summary: US strikes perimeter of Iran’s Bushehr nuclear plant, Iranian state media reports The United States targeted the perimeter of Iran’s Bushehr nuclear power plant on Thursday, Iranian state media reported, citing Ehsan Jahanian, deputy governor of Bushehr province. Jahanian said several areas across the province were targeted, including the area around the nuclear plant, a military base in the town of Choghadak and a fishing pier in southern Bushehr. He said there were no immediate reports of casualties. Residents in Choghadak, located just over 20km (12 miles) from the Bushehr plant, reported hearing several explosions. The Bushehr facility, Iran’s only civilian nuclear power plant, has previously been affected by strikes in the area during the ongoing Middle East war.

items.title: Iran warns of retaliation if IAEA adopts resolution against Tehran
items.summary: Iran warns of retaliation if IAEA adopts resolution against Tehran Iran has warned that it will take reciprocal action if the UN nuclear watchdog adopts a resolution against Tehran, foreign ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei said on Monday. Speaking at a press briefing, Baghaei criticised European states seeking a resolution against Iran, calling their approach “irrational” given that the ongoing US-Iran war has made several Iranian nuclear facilities inaccessible to international inspectors. His comments come as the US, Britain, France and Germany push for a resolution at the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) over Iran’s lack of cooperation and access to its nuclear sites. Iran has restricted IAEA access to facilities affected by previous strikes, arguing that normal safeguarding arrangements have become impractical under wartime conditions. The dispute has deepened concerns over the status of Iran’s enriched uranium stockpile and the international community’s ability to verify the nature of its nuclear programme.

items.title: Massie, Kent join ex-officials lighting up Ron Paul ‘revolution’
items.summary: In his first non-Congressional  public speech since his Republican primary loss to Ed Gallrhein, Thomas Massie brought some of the loudest energy to the Ron Paul Institute’s Washington conference on Saturday. He was full of jokes and promise for the future. Massie said he was not interested in mourning the defeat and declared that he was, in a way, happy he had lost. items.summary: The Falklands dispute: What’s it got to do with Israel and the US? Argentina has restated its claim to sovereignty over the Falkland Islands, a small rocky archipelago in the South Atlantic that is owned by the UK . Javier Milei, the far-right president of Argentina, said in a national address on Thursday that the "winds of change" favoured his country’s claim to the islands, and threatened sanctions on oil firms that seek to drill in the territory’s waters. "We need to recover these islands which are nationally relevant," he said. The announcement comes days after US President Donald Trump suggested that he is reviewing the US position on UK sovereignty, known in Argentina as Las Islas Malvinas. “I always review every position - that’s just one of many,” Trump told reporters in the White House. “The UK’s got some problems, but they’ll get solved." The future of the sparsely inhabited islands has been speculated on for months amid tensions between Washington and London about UK military commitments, including the war on Iran . Miles de kilómetros separan la capital española de esta ciudad de la India, en la que se levanta el corazón espiritual del sijismo, una religión nacida de un acercamiento de posturas entre el hinduismo y el islam. Cada día, los sij de esta región se reúnen para comer en la monumental infraestructura que constituye el Templo Dorado, donde llenan sus bandejas sin coste ni distinción por edad, género o religión. Lo mismo sucede, en proporciones contenidas, en una nave industrial de Villaverde que esconde el único templo sij de la capital, el Gurudwara Nanaksar Sahib de Madrid. Con el mismo espíritu que en la India, pero en esplendor y dimensiones reducidos, este lugar ofrece comidas gratuitas cada domingo a unas pocas decenas de personas.Laura, madrileña de Las Rozas y bautizada en el catolicismo, es una habitual en el lugar desde que, hace más de un año, un viaje a la India despertó en ella una nueva forma de concebir su fe. «Aquí aprendo cómo llegar a dios, que es el mismo para todos», sostiene. items.title: Amerikaans vliegdekschip USS Abraham Lincoln verlaat Thailand
items.summary: Het Amerikaanse vliegdekschip USS Abraham Lincoln is na vijf dagen vertrokken uit Thailand. Bijna 5000 bemanningsleden zijn meer dan negen maanden na hun vertrek uit de Verenigde Staten onderweg naar de haven van San Diego. De afgelopen vijf dagen lag de Lincoln in de Thaise haven Laem Chabang, dicht bij de badplaats Pattaya. De badplaats is Amerikaanse soldaten niet onbekend: tijdens de Vietnamoorlog werd het een bekende plek voor het zogenoemde R&R ( Rest and Relaxation) , oftewel: een vakantie voor militairen. De badplaats had daarvoor voorbereidingen getroffen: er werd onder meer een prostitutieverbod ingesteld en er werden extra agenten ingezet. Lokale verslaggevers melden dat het bezoek relatief soepel is verlopen. Soldaten genoten van voetspa's, winkelen en roomservice. Volgens persbureau AFP zijn twee leden van het leger teruggestuurd naar het schip na een dronken ruzie. The renewed clashes in Yemen's southwest over control of a gateway to the Red Sea came after Friday saw some of the deadliest fighting in years, following the collapse in July of a 2022 ceasefire. According to three Yemeni military sources, 26 government troops were killed during several hours of fighting in the country's southwest, while medical and military sources from the Iran-backed Houthis said 31 rebel fighters were killed. One medical source in the government-held city of Taiz said a missile strike also killed six civilians travelling by bus and wounded seven others. A government official blamed the strike on the bus, travelling between Taiz and the seat of Yemen's internationally recognised government in Aden, on the Houthis. items.title: Iran condemns US attacks on commercial vessels as war crimes
items.summary: Iran condemns US attacks on commercial vessels as war crimes Iran has accused the United States of violating international law by attacking its commercial vessels and imposing a naval blockade against the country. “The Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic of Iran strongly condemns the aggressive US action of attacking Iranian commercial vessels,” the Foreign Ministry said. Tehran described the strikes as part of Washington’s wider military campaign and “economic war” against Iran. It said the attacks violated the UN Charter and endangered international peace, security and commercial shipping. The ministry pledged to “firmly defend its sovereignty and national interests” against US aggression, state-sponsored terrorism, the continuing blockade and the “harassment of commercial ships”. It added that Washington and its allies would bear responsibility for any consequences arising from continued US “aggressive and interventionist actions” in the region.

items.title: Top US military officials face lie-detectors in leak investigation: reports
items.summary: Top US military officials face lie-detectors in leak investigation: reports The Pentagon has begun subjecting senior military officials to lie-detector tests as part of an investigation into who leaked details about US munitions stockpiles, US media reported. Reports in July said the US was rationing some munitions, particularly missile interceptors, amid concerns over supplies following months of war with Iran. Trump administration officials strongly rejected the claims. President Donald Trump said the US had "a lot of ammunition, different types", while acknowledging that the military would like more of "some of the more sophisticated stuff". The New York Times reported late on Friday that around 50 members of the military’s Joint Staff, the Pentagon’s planning and advisory body, were being required to undergo polygraph tests as part of an investigation into the leak.

items.title: US military says it has destroyed three Iranian oil tankers
items.summary: US military says it has destroyed three Iranian oil tankers The US military said it had struck and destroyed three oil tankers linked to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) after US warships came under Iranian fire. "Following Iran’s failed attacks, CENTCOM permanently disabled the IRGC crude oil carriers M/T Downy off the coast of Kharg Island and M/T Stark 1 near Jask," Central Command (Centcom) said in a statement on X. "American forces also completely destroyed the unladen crude oil carrier M/T Kylo … in the Gulf of Oman, striking the vessel in multiple critical locations to render it inoperable after the crew was directed to abandon ship," it continued. Video released by Centcom showed huge fireballs and thick plumes of flames erupting as projectiles struck the vessels. The three ships targeted were "part of a multibillion-dollar shadow network that funds the IRGC and its regional proxies", it said. "Iran has no means by which to defend them," it added.

items.summary: US diesel prices hit record $5.85 a gallon The price of diesel hit a new record Friday in the United States, as disruption from the US war with Iran squeezes voters. The cost is now $5.85 a gallon, up from $3.71 a year ago, the AAA motorists' association said. Diesel is used by farmers to run equipment, and it also powers the trucks needed to bring food to grocery stores. US farmers faced a double whammy of surging fertiliser and diesel prices as the spring planting season got underway. The Independent Grocers Alliance estimates that fuel-related costs can account for 15 to 30 percent of the total cost for some food products. Besides diesel, the cost of regular gasoline is also notably higher at an average of $4.15 per gallon, compared with $3.20 last year. (Reporting by AFP)

Four vessels entered the Middle East Gulf and one exited, using a mix of Iranian, Omani and negotiated routes. Two of the crossings involved shadow vessels, while one involved a sanctioned vessel. Kpler said the figure remained preliminary, noting that additional “dark” crossings could be retrospectively identified and added as new confirmation data becomes available. Activity through the Bab el-Mandeb was comparatively stable, with 35 confirmed crossings, up 2.9 percent day on day. Nineteen vessels entered the Red Sea and 16 exited. No dark transits were recorded, while the International Maritime Organization verified no additional attacks. items.title: World food prices at highest since 2022, says UN
items.summary: World food prices at highest since 2022, says UN World food prices rose in August to their highest since late 2022, impacted partly by the war on Iran, the United Nations' Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) said on Friday. Extreme heat and drought in Europe, the threat of a severe El Nino weather pattern and trade upheaval caused by the Ukraine and Iran wars have unsettled agricultural markets, pushing grain prices to three-year highs and sugar to a one-year peak, the agency said. The FAO Food Price Index, which tracks monthly changes in a basket of internationally traded food commodities, averaged 133.3 points in August, up from July's revised reading of 130.8. That was the highest score since November 2022, though nearly 17 percent below a record peak from March 2022, after Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine, Reuters reported. Escalating attacks in the Black Sea have curtailed grain shipments from Russia and Ukraine, while the war on Iran is still straining flows of fertiliser for crops.

items.title: Adam Telle appointed as acting US Army Secretary, Trump says
items.summary: Adam Telle appointed as acting US Army Secretary, Trump says US President Donald Trump said that he was appointing Adam Telle, assistant secretary of the Army for civil works, as the acting US Army Secretary. This came after the White House confirmed earlier this week that former army secretary, Dan Driscoll, submitted his resignation. Driscoll’s departure came following reports of increasing tensions with Secretary of War Pete Hegseth as well as signs of unease in the Pentagon over how the Trump administration is prosecuting the war on Iran. The heads of the army, navy and air force, and the four-star commanders overseeing US operations throughout Europe, Asia and Latin America, have warned Hegseth that any prolonging of major operations would weaken the Washington's ability to confront other foes, the Washington Post reported on Monday.

items.title: Iran says oil industry circumventing US blockade
items.summary: Iran says oil industry circumventing US blockade Iran’s oil industry continues to find ways around a US military blockade of the country’s ports and vessels, Petroleum Minister Mohsen Paknejad told the Iranian Students News Agency (ISNA). “We are pursuing various strategies and have taken measures to overcome the blockade,” Paknejad said, describing the situation as difficult. He said US forces had attacked Kharg Island off Iran’s southwestern coast “more than 550 times” during the first 40 days of the conflict. Iran exported about 90 percent of its crude oil from the island before the war.

A cargo jet, meanwhile, may have struck a second drone shortly after takeoff, forcing an abrupt landing, and investigators found a third drone laden with military explosives nearby. items.title: ‘I would rather die than return to France’: the brutal reality of the UK’s one in, one out scheme
items.summary: Aso and Baran fled Iran, crossed the Channel together and were both returned to France. After risking their lives to reach Britain again, the friends found themselves facing very different fates At the end of last year, two men fled Iran. Aso and Baran* were strangers at the time. The way their stories would cross, then diverge, reveals the cruel arbitrariness of the UK asylum system in general, and the government’s controversial one in, one out scheme in particular. Before he left Iran, Aso, 28, had converted from Islam to Christianity, putting his life in imminent danger. “I had to keep my conversion to Christianity a secret,” he says. “I knew if I was caught, I risked being executed by the Iranian regime … one of my relatives, who I trusted, paid smugglers to get me out last November.” Continue reading...

items.title: Iran urges UN action over deadly US attack on wedding
items.summary: Iran urges UN action over deadly US attack on wedding Iran has accused the United States of committing a “war crime” by bombing a wedding gathering in southern Hormozgan province. In a letter to the United Nations Security Council, Iranian Ambassador Gholamhossein Darzi described the attack on civilians as an “appalling” and “egregious” crime that violated international law. Darzi urged the UN to “hold the United States fully responsible” and ensure it brings “an end to its acts of aggression” against Iran. The US strike killed at least four people, including two children, and wounded 50 others at the wedding in Sirik. Iran’s Health Ministry said recent US air strikes had killed at least 18 people and wounded another 142.

items.title: 'Inappropriate to say': Trump may still be considering CIA-led uprising in Iran
items.summary: 'Inappropriate to say': Trump may still be considering CIA-led uprising in Iran US President Donald Trump on Wednesday said it "wouldn't be appropriate to say" if he would greenlight the CIA arming Iranians to encourage a violent uprising, a day after he asked on his TruthSocial account, "When are the Iranian people going to rise up and fight?" Trump was taking unscheduled questions in the Oval Office, after the US unleashed a barrage of strikes on Iran's southern coast on Tuesday, killing 18 people, including two children at a wedding. "Will you send the CIA in to arm Iranians?" a reporter asked the president. "I'd love to tell you that, but it wouldn't be appropriate to say," Trump responded. "But I mean, I understand their plight. They're being shot... They have close to 65,000 protesters killed." It remains unclear where that figure is sourced, given Trump has previously floated figures between 25,000 and 80,000 during the anti-government protests in Iran early this year. items.summary: This summer the Pentagon handed NATO members a questionnaire asking whether they support in part, “U.S. foreign policy priorities.” Dubbed a “loyalty test” in the press, it was seen by many Europeans as the most recent sign that the alliance is coming apart because of American petulance. Yet what is actually happening is that the U.S. is putting stress on an inherently flawed and now exhausted form of alliance politics. The roots of the present discord were planted not in the 2024 reelection of President Donald Trump, but in the moment of NATO's Cold War triumph thirty years earlier. items.summary: UN chief urges US, Iran to 'return urgently to diplomacy' after renewed attacks UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres on Wednesday expressed "grave concern" after renewed strikes between the US and Iran, and condemned all attacks against civilians. "The secretary-general is deeply alarmed by reports of civilian casualties, including a strike that reportedly hit a wedding ceremony in Iran," UN spokesperson Stephane Dujarric said during a news conference. "The secretary-general condemns all attacks against civilians," Dujarric said. "He recalls that all parties must respect their obligations under international humanitarian law, including the principles of distinction, proportionality, and precaution." He added that the UN chief urged Washington and Tehran to "return urgently to diplomacy," adding that a "comprehensive and durable settlement can be achieved only through dialog and negotiations".

Trump was taking unscheduled questions in the Oval Office, after the US unleashed a barrage of strikes on Iran's southern coast on Tuesday, killing 18 people, including two children at a wedding. "Will you send the CIA in to arm Iranians?" a reporter asked the president. "I'd love to tell you that, but it wouldn't be appropriate to say," Trump responded. It remains unclear where that figure is sourced, given Trump has previously floated figures between 25,000 and 80,000 during the anti-government protests in Iran early this year. items.title: Trump’s Saudi nuke agreement may prolong the Iran war
items.summary: A final deal between the United States and Iran is slipping further out of reach. Since the Memorandum of Understanding collapsed in July, the prospects for reviving it have deteriorated by the day. While Tehran publicly demands a return to the MOU, Trump’s current position is that even if Iran reopened the Strait of Hormuz, he would neither return to the agreement nor lift the blockade on Iran. And even in the unlikely event that he did, the MOU could not come back into force as long as Israel continues to bombard Lebanon. Iran is unlikely to accept an MOU minus Lebanon: its demand for a regional ceasefire is non-negotiable. But even if these obstacles were resolved, profound differences over the nuclear issue would remain. And those differences have now grown dramatically more severe because of Trump’s nuclear agreement with Saudi Arabia. The details of the deal were just made public, and Kelsey Davenport at the Arms Control Association has published an excellent FAQ addressing its most important aspects. Tuesday’s spike in gilt yields, taking the UK’s 30-year borrowing costs to their highest level since 1998 , was part of an international sell-off of government debt . The main contributors are well known. The Iran war, by increasing the cost of energy, has overturned the comforting start-of-the-year thesis of falling global inflation and interest rates. A plunging Japanese yen has kicked away another assumed source of financial stability. The US treasury secretary, Scott Bessent, hasn’t calmed nerves with his solo, and so far futile, attempt to bring down US yields . items.summary: Het Nationaal Warmtefonds heeft tot nu toe al meer leningen verstrekt dan in heel 2025. Bij het fonds kunnen mensen geld lenen om hun huis te verduurzamen. Van januari tot en met augustus werden ruim 22.000 leningen verstrekt. In heel 2025 waren dat er 21.000. De lening wordt gebruikt voor bijvoorbeeld muur- en dakisolatie, isolerend glas of zonnepanelen. De piek heeft te maken met de oorlog in het Midden-Oosten, die de VS en Israël eind februari ontketenden met hun aanvallen op Iran. Als tegenzet gooide Iran de Straat van Hormuz dicht, de zeestraat waardoor tot die tijd een vijfde van de wereldwijde olie en aardgas werd vervoerd. Door die blokkade zijn de energieprijzen fors gestegen. "De piek was vanaf het moment dat de oorlog begon", vertelt Katinka Huiberts, bestuurslid bij het Nationaal Warmtefonds. "De aanvragen begonnen toen heel scherp te stijgen." Die stijging zette het hele voorjaar tot de zomer door, zegt Huiberts. items.title: Why are so many Vance allies leaving the administration?
items.summary: Army Secretary Dan Driscoll resigned this week, raising a flurry of questions about whether his departure is part of a larger political reordering that has pushed skeptics of President Donald Trump’s war policies to the margins. A long-time friend of Vice President JD Vance, Driscoll drew widespread praise for his efforts to modernize the Army. But he has clashed with Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth, particularly over the latter’s firing of numerous senior military officials , including Army and Air Force generals and the Secretary of the Navy. Driscoll brought his concerns about these firings directly to Trump last week, who said he was unaware of how many officers had been purged, according to the Atlantic. Driscoll’s departure is the latest in a string of recent high-profile exits by Vance’s allies and ideological fellow travelers, including Director of National Intelligence Tulsi Gabbard, Deputy National Security Adviser Andy Baker, White House Director of Legislative Affairs James Braid, and Director of the National Counterterrorism Center Joe Kent. items.title: Por qué el país más rico del mundo no puede defender sus infraestructuras vitales
items.summary: El agua es una vulnerabilidad estratégica, un hecho que no es ninguna novedad para los mandos militares. Cuando los ostrogodos quisieron paralizar Roma en el año 537, destruyeron sus acueductos. Más recientemente, las infraestructuras hidráulicas han sido un objetivo importante en el conflicto de Estados Unidos con Irán, a pesar de que las leyes internacionales clasifican este tipo de ataques como posibles crímenes de guerra. En marzo, Donald Trump amenazó con «destruir por completo… posiblemente todas» las instalaciones de desalinización de Irán, que son esenciales para la vida en las áridas provincias del sur del país. Irán afirma que una de esas instalaciones fue bombardeada en la isla de Qeshm. Bahréin, Kuwait y Emiratos Árabes Unidos han sufrido ataques con misiles contra sus propias plantas de agua, que se presume que procedían de Irán.Por tanto, fue digno de mención, aunque no debería haber sido una sorpresa, que las propias instalaciones de agua de Estados Unidos fueran objeto de un ataque este verano. items.title: Gulf states struggle to recover economically after 6 months of war
items.summary: The Persian Gulf’s extraordinary wealth has long rested on an assumption of stability. The past six months of war have shattered that certainty, exposing a fundamental weakness in Gulf economic models: producing oil and gas is only half the equation when infrastructure and access to global markets can be disrupted. Ports, airports, power grids, desalination plants, financial centers, and tourism hubs are all vulnerable to the same regional shocks. The energy sector is particularly exposed, with damaged oil and gas facilities potentially taking months or longer to repair. Yet restoring production may prove easier than restoring confidence that Gulf exports can reliably reach global markets. Each Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) state enters this new era from a different starting point. Qatar, Kuwait and Bahrain are particularly exposed because of their reliance on Gulf maritime routes, including the Strait of Hormuz. The Gulf monarchies’ experience of the Iran war makes such a realignment appear plausible. Despite their decades-long partnership with Washington, they became targets of Iranian drone and missile attacks that caused considerable damage to the region’s energy infrastructure and severely disrupted energy exports, as the Strait of Hormuz was effectively closed. The Trump administration appears to have taken little account of their security interests . Nevertheless, three factors make an end to their close ties with Washington unlikely. Limits of realignment First, the Gulf monarchies have no viable alternative to the United States as a security guarantor. items.title: After Iran, US signals major security shift in the Middle East
items.summary: When President Donald Trump congratulated Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan for signing the Mecca Pact, describing it as a “BIG, BOLD, IMPORTANT FIRST STEP,” he was not simply trafficking in diplomatic pleasantries. The Trump administration also tacitly endorsed a multilateral, Saudi-led maritime initiative to protect shipping in the Red Sea, sending senior U.S. military officials to the meeting where the arrangement was agreed to. The thread running through both initiatives is clear: regional states taking greater responsibility for their own security. Behind Trump’s flattery, something more important appears to be taking shape. According to Pentagon planning reported by the Washington Post, the Defense Department is exploring a broader reduction of its forces in the Persian Gulf, which would entail moving units, command centers and aerial capabilities west toward Jordan, Israel and Saudi Arabia’s Red Sea coast. items.title: La modernité de l’Iranienne Forough Farrokhzâd, poétesse rebelle et lumineuse
items.summary: Forough Farrokhzâd est l’une des plus grandes figures de la poésie iranienne du dernier siècle. Sa disparition brutale en 1967, à l’âge de 32 ans, fut une perte immense pour son pays, pour la littérature. Sa voix, « fusionnée dans les atomes du temps » comme elle l’a écrit, continue de se faire entendre à travers sa poésie sublime et tragique. « J’irai jusqu’au rivage du soleil » est le titre du volume en traduction française de ses poésies complètes, paru cette année dans la prestigieuse collection Poésie/Gallimard.
